9.author: St. Basil the Great
9.text: Basil's treatise On the Holy Spirit defended the Spirit's full divinity against those who reduced Him to a creature. Commenting on Paul's language of life 'in the Spirit,' Basil argues that the Spirit dwells in the faithful as God Himself, not as an outside influence, and so unites them to Christ and through Christ to the Father. The doxology the Church still uses, 'Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit,' is in no small part Basil's gift, defended in this very treatise as the proper confession of the Spirit's equal honor with the Father and the Son.
